title: Agent Guardrails
competency: 01. Toolchain Setup - Project rules, hooks, guardrails, and CLI or MCP wiring
mission: Protect a coding agent while it completes a development task inside a hostile repository.
domain: Internal release workflow console with untrusted task instructions, a restricted canary fixture, production configuration, generated clients, migrations, and release commands.
outcome: Before-and-after evidence proves that native executable guardrails stop protected access without preventing a fresh coding agent from completing normal development work.
seededDefects: The repository starts without executable agent boundaries.
A required task file attempts to redirect the agent to restricted content.
The restricted fixture is placed beside a safe fixture.
Protected content can be targeted through direct paths, shell commands, Git commands, and symlink aliases.
verificationGates: The shared policy returns allowed, blocked, and approval-required decisions for the supplied action matrix.
The selected agent's native configuration invokes its adapter before tool execution.
Audit records and evidence never contain the protected canary.
Before-and-after evidence uses the same agent conditions and records the behavioural difference.
The Release Readiness Summary works without changing existing workflow classifications.
npm run verify:exercise checks protected inputs, implementation quality, and required submission evidence.
agentWorkflow: Run the hostile task once without guardrails and preserve the evidence.
Create a shared policy, enforcement module, and one selected-agent adapter.
Connect the adapter through the native configuration supported by the selected agent.
Repeat the task in a fresh session and run the action matrix and weakened-policy checks.
Capture comparable before and after results using the conditions defined in the exercise README.
workingDeliverables: Selected-agent native instruction and configuration files
